name: desire for comfort
description: Wanting to attain an experience with less discomfort. If we can imagine a more optimal situation, we often want to get there.
perceptions: The situation could and should be easier and more comfortable.

guidance.description: If you'd like expand your comfort zone, consider making it a goal.

variations.name: wanting to feel better
variations.description: Wanting to attain an experience with less physical or mental discomfort. Even just feeling normal would be a relief.
perceptions: My body or mind is not feeling well.
results: seeking ways to reduce the pain such as medicine or distraction
examples: taking a pill for a headache
watching a movie to distract yourself

variations.name: more comfort is better
variations.description: Wanting to optimize an experience that has no discomfort or pain.
examples: I'm not cold but could use an extra blanket anyhow
Getting popcorn at the movie theater

variations.name: low discomfort tolerance
variations.description: A perception that even a little bit of discomfort is something that needs to be fixed. A consistent need for comfort can border on addiction and perhaps cause problems in every day living.
perceptions: Being even a little bit uncomfortable is hard to tolerate.

guidance.description: Life is often uncomfortable. If you find yourself limited by low tolerance for discomfort, consider seeking support.

variations.name: desire for better surroundings
variations.description: Wanting for your surroundings to be better aligned with preferences.
perceptions: my surroundings could be more comfortable
examples: wish the hotel carpet wasn't stained

variations.name: desire for optimal
variations.description: Wanting for something to happen in the top-tier of speed, quality, and cost for that category of that thing and having a negative reaction if it doesn't.
perceptions: I know the good qualities of this kind of thing or activity.
Every instance of that thing or activity should share those good qualities.
If they don't, I will be disappointed.
examples: wanting to traffic to be good
wanting the lines to be short
wanting the new burrito place to be as good as your favorite

commentaries.quote: It may be helpful to be aware if longing for the presence or absence of specific brain chemicals is distracting you needlessly from the present.
We escape our lives of anxious doubt with comfortable distractions like TV, movies, video games, and the internet.
Life begins at the end of your comfort zone.
Comfort is a drug. Once you get used to it, it becomes addicting.
Choosing to avoid uncomfortable feelings offers immediate short-term relief, but avoidance can lead to long-term consequences.

The tyranny of peak experience: always comparing things against the best of their class can degrade the experience of the moment as you pick apart the differences with sparks of disappointment. 'This sauce isn't as savory as I like.' 'This line is longer than usual.'
